facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 8:00 AM ET

The 2026 US Open women's final is officially set.

On Thursday night at Arthur Ashe Stadium, No. 1 seed Aryna Sabalenka dismantled Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2, and No. 2 Elena Rybakina rallied past Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4, to set up a blockbuster women's final on Saturday.

Sabalenka was clinical against Pegula, attacking the American's second serve and using her serve-plus-one strategy to devastating effect. Pegula — who had made three consecutive US Open semifinals — could not find her best tennis when it mattered most. Sabalenka's 7-5 win in the first set was the turning point, and the second set was all business.

The Rybakina-Gauff match was more dramatic. Gauff took the opening set 6-3 and looked like she might pull off a massive upset against the new world No. 1. But Rybakina, who has faced adversity throughout this tournament, found another gear. She took the second set 6-4 and then won the third 6-4 to close it out.

Both women were on the right side of the draw and they delivered. The stage is set for Saturday.

---

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 10:30 AM ET

Saturday's US Open women's final has everything.

Aryna Sabalenka is chasing history. She won the 2023 and 2024 US Open titles, and a third consecutive crown would place her among the most exclusive company in the Open Era. She has been dominant this fortnight, dropping just one set in her run to the final.

Standing in her way: Elena Rybakina, the sport's new No. 1.

Rybakina won the 2026 Australian Open in January — defeating Sabalenka in the final — and now arrives at Arthur Ashe as the top-ranked player in the world. A victory Saturday would mean she holds two of the year's four Grand Slam titles and sweeps the 2026 hardcourt majors. That would be a statement season by any measure.

Their rivalry is rich. Sabalenka leads the overall head-to-head 10-7, but the Grand Slam final record is split 1-1. The data point that matters most: in 14 of their last 17 meetings, the player who won the first set won the match. First set everything.

This is a final worthy of the US Open. Saturday at Arthur Ashe. Don't look away.

---

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 6:00 PM ET

Tonight at Arthur Ashe, American tennis makes history.

Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe — two Americans, both from this country, both raised watching their sport be dominated by Spaniards, Serbs, and Russians — will play each other in the US Open men's semifinals. The winner goes to Sunday's final. An American man WILL be in that final.

The last American man to win a Grand Slam title was Andy Roddick. That was 2003. The sport has changed completely since then. A 23-year wait is about to end.

Shelton's path to tonight was the stuff of movies. He defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in five breathless sets, with the match ending at 3:33 AM in the latest finish in US Open history. He was 0-17 against top-3 opponents before that night. Now he is one win from a Grand Slam final at age 22.

Tiafoe has been electric at Flushing Meadows. He is a perfect 10-0 at Louis Armstrong Stadium across his entire career, and he dispatched Daniil Medvedev in the round of 16 — his first career win over the Russian — on his way to the semis. This is his third US Open semifinal in five years.

Tonight is the match. Both are playing for more than themselves.

---

article.headline: Shelton vs. Tiafoe: The All-American US Open Semifinal That Changes Everything

stories.title: The 23-Year Wait — American Men's Grand Slam Drought About to End (TIER 1)

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
An American man WILL win a Grand Slam title on Sunday.

First time since Andy Roddick won the 2003 US Open. The 23-year drought ends this weekend — Shelton vs. Tiafoe is the men's final.

#USOpen #AmericanTennis

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 12:30 PM ET

A 23-year drought. That's how long American men have waited to win a Grand Slam title.

Andy Roddick won the 2003 US Open, defeating Juan Carlos Ferrero in straight sets. Since that September afternoon in Flushing Meadows, American men have reached Grand Slam finals — Taylor Fritz did it at the 2024 US Open — but the title has always gone elsewhere.

Not this time.

With Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe both winning their quarterfinals, the 2026 US Open men's final is guaranteed to be all-American. The winner will be the first American man to lift a Grand Slam trophy in 23 years.

Think about what that means. Jannik Sinner, the world No. 1, didn't make it. Carlos Alcaraz, the defending champion, fell at 3:33 AM to a 22-year-old from Atlanta who had never beaten a top-3 player before that night. The draw opened up, and two Americans walked through.

Shelton is 22. Tiafoe is 28. Different generations of the same dream. Tonight they play each other, and on Sunday, one of them makes history.

---

article.headline: The 23-Year American Men's Grand Slam Drought Is About to End

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Alexander Zverev won Roland Garros in June — his first Grand Slam title.

Today he faces Khachanov in the US Open semifinals. Win this, and he could hold two majors in 2026.

That's the kind of season we're watching. #USOpen

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 3:00 PM ET

Before the American showdown tonight, there's another compelling men's semifinal to watch.

Alexander Zverev — the reigning Roland Garros champion — faces Karen Khachanov in the first match on Arthur Ashe this afternoon, no earlier than 3 PM ET.

Zverev has been the world's best men's player this year, winning Roland Garros in June for his first Grand Slam title. A win today would put him one match from winning two majors in a single calendar year — something he has never done.

Khachanov is in his third Grand Slam semifinal (2022 US Open, 2023 Australian Open) and has never gone further. He advanced when his quarterfinal opponent, Alexander Blockx, retired in the third set. Whether that affects his match sharpness for today is an open question.

The first set, as always with Zverev, is key. If he gets out front, he rarely lets go.

---
